what: ICON runs clinical trials for drug companies. It recruits patients, manages the sites and collects the data that a new medicine needs to be approved, on contract rather than doing its own research.
customers: Large pharmaceutical companies and biotechs that outsource trials instead of keeping the staff in house.
money: running phase I to IV trials, patient recruitment and data management
moat: A global network of trial sites and investigators, and multi-year master agreements with the largest drug companies, which take years of delivery to win.
risks: Biotech funding has been weak, and small biotechs are a large source of new trial bookings
Large customers have been cancelling or delaying trials, which shows up in the backlog before revenue
76 times earnings on a business whose revenue has been flat around $8.2B for three years
opportunities: Free cash flow of $857M against $448M of reported net income, so the cash is far better than the earnings
Analysts see about 22% upside, with 17 covering the stock
Drug companies have been cutting internal research staff, which pushes more trial work to outside providers
watch: Net new business bookings and the book-to-bill ratio, which lead revenue by about a year.
